beats.headline: Fight mosquitoes with mosquitoes.
beats.text: Male mosquitoes carrying Wolbachia don’t bite. When they mate with wild females, the eggs don’t hatch.

coverage.note: households targeted by end-2026: half of Singapore’s households

beats.headline: Day one.
beats.text: On 18 October, NEA’s Environmental Health Institute releases about 3,000 males at Braddell Heights.

beats.headline: Half isn’t enough.
beats.text: Phase 1 halves mosquito numbers. But mosquitoes from next door move in, and a few females slip through sorting.

coverage.note: study sites, not counted in households

beats.headline: New partner.
beats.text: Phase 2 begins in April. In September, Verily’s Debug team joins as a collaborator.

beats.headline: Past 90%.
beats.text: Phase 3 cuts the urban Aedes aegypti population by more than 90% across 144 residential blocks.

beats.headline: The worst year.
beats.text: Singapore’s largest dengue outbreak: 35,000+ cases. Releases cover about 8% of HDB blocks.

beats.headline: Fewer cases.
beats.text: Study sites in four towns: up to 98% fewer mosquitoes and up to 88% fewer dengue cases. Observational, not yet randomised.

coverage.note: HDB blocks in Yishun and Tampines by June 2021

beats.headline: The trial.
beats.text: 15 areas, about 724,000 residents. Eight are picked at random for releases. Seven get none.

beats.headline: A million residents.
beats.text: Releases now reach more than 300,000 households and about 30% of HDB blocks.

beats.headline: 96% say yes.
beats.text: In community surveys, 96% of residents accept releases in their neighbourhood. The trial ends in September.

beats.headline: Quietest since 2018.
beats.text: 4,036 dengue cases nationwide. MSE credits no major outbreak, a global dip and mosquito control by everyone.

beats.headline: The verdict.
beats.text: 71–72% lower dengue risk in release areas. 6% of tests positive, vs 21% in control areas.
2,351 estimated dengue cases averted during the trial (95% CI 1,968–2,735). Same trial, second analysis.
